headline: Highest risk is medium: shared OAuth/API surfaces and broad egress create plausible leakage and conflict paths, but no direct shared workspace or documented interaction is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can expose outputs through OIDC/OAuth2 and ForwardAuth, while Opik consumes REST API inputs. No shared filesystem or parser bridge is documented, so a prompt-injection path is not default. The plausible bridge is manual or integration-driven, making blast radius limited and interaction uncertain.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into Opik prompts or evaluation inputs
IF a shared middleware forwards Authelia responses into Opik without sanitization
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste bridge between Authelia outputs and Opik inputs
Add a sanitizer that strips instruction-like text before Opik ingestion
Use a fixed schema for forwarded Authelia responses
Review any ForwardAuth integration for untrusted content handling

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Authelia handles authentication flows while Opik is an observability/evaluation system that may transmit inputs over REST. No data classes are listed, so leakage is not proven, but the pair has a plausible default path for sensitive auth metadata to leave the local boundary.
conditions: IF Authelia forwards identity or session metadata into Opik logs or traces
IF Opik sends captured request/response payloads to a third-party backend
mitigations: Redact tokens and headers before Opik ingestion
Restrict Authelia logs to non-sensitive fields
Turn off payload capture in Opik for auth flows
Verify both systems use separate credentials and tenants

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and API integrations, and Opik exposes a REST API, so overlapping writes to shared remote resources are possible only if an operator wires them together. Neither profile shows filesystem write, subprocess spawning, or shared mutable storage, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or datastore
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Use distinct namespaces or projects
Enable optimistic locking on shared resources
Document ownership of each mutable endpoint

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and Opik can ingest REST data for evaluation or observability, so one agent's output could become the other's input. There is no evidence of verification between them, but also no proof that Opik acts autonomously on Authelia's outputs, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Opik treats Authelia-produced records as authoritative without validation
IF Authelia-derived events are used to trigger downstream actions in Opik
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Opik consumes Authelia outputs
Require human review for any action derived from auth events
Tag Authelia-originated records as untrusted
Add schema checks for all forwarded events

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no sensitive data classes, certifications, or residency constraints, so no concrete compliance breach is shown. The only relevant concern is that Authelia's authentication data could be logged or forwarded into Opik, but the profiles do not establish regulated-data handling, so this remains a low, conditional risk.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is routed from Authelia into Opik logs
IF an operator stores EU PII or PHI in either system without a matching policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated fields to Opik
Set short log retention on both systems
Review data residency settings before deployment
Document which data classes each system may process
